concept.sourceKind: Original generated concept, explicitly approved by the user
concept.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one premium industrial-design concept sheet redesigning the anti-gravity racing craft in the two supplied screenshots. These screenshots show front and rear of the SAME existing Kestrel and are reference inputs only: retain its pearl ceramic / graphite / brushed titanium / restrained vermilion racing identity and twin propulsion concept, but substantially redesign its silhouette. The user's primary request is a more futuristic jet-like craft, less bulky, less bubbly. Make this a credible original racing machine for an interactive high-speed 3D game.

Shape direction: a long, lean, sharply tapered central fuselage with a decisive pointed wedge nose; roughly 2.3 times as long as wide. Very low, elongated dark canopy integrated flush into a defined central spine, with crisp edges rather than a tall bubble. Thin swept shoulders / compact delta-like body chines, negative space beneath the side edges, tightly packaged mechanical underside. Short swept stabilizing surfaces and restrained rear canted fins can give a jet-derived silhouette. Twin compact propulsion units blended into the rear fuselage, ending in angular titanium exhaust apertures with restrained cyan active cores. Eliminate the reference's oversized freestanding circular drums and swollen rounded side shells. Use sculpted hard-surface planes, clean chamfers, a few intentional seams, recessed vents and credible construction, not random greeble or excessive tiny panels. Slim integrated anti-gravity hardware on the underside. No wheels, landing gear, weapons or missiles. Not a copied recognizable franchise craft. Preserve the original small 07 marking and subtle vermilion stripes; do not invent sponsor branding.

Composition: polished landscape design board on a neutral warm-gray studio background. One large beautifully lit front three-quarter hero view occupies the left two-thirds, showing the entire ship with ample margin, hovering low with a soft grounding shadow. Two smaller clearly separated views of the exact SAME consistent design on the right: an upper top-down silhouette and a lower rear three-quarter/chase-oriented view, making the slim rear and propulsion readable. No environment, track, game HUD, speed lines, motion blur or cinematic distractions. Small restrained typography only: 'KESTREL / CONCEPT 01' and 'FRONT', 'TOP', 'REAR' adjacent to the appropriate views. The craft itself is the focus.

Finish: realistic AAA vehicle concept rendering with physically plausible ceramic, satin composite and brushed metal, neutral studio key/fill and subtle warm highlights; deliberate sleek aerospace surfacing, muscular but lightweight and elegant. This is concept exploration for a replacement model, not a screenshot of the existing game.
concept.referenceInputs: Two local front/rear stills of the earlier original Kestrel from .experiments/ship-gate2/refined/

model.authorship: Original component geometry authored for this project against the approved concept. No downloaded model, external texture or font asset.
model.userDirection: More futuristic jet, less bulky and bubbly; delegated Blender refinement with independent critic target of at least 9/10, bounded to eight formal rounds.
model.materials: Original authored metre-space ceramic, graphite and directional metal graphs with sparse contact scuffs, 6.5 cm cavity dirt and aft-localized heat tint; Blender-baked color, roughness, tangent normals and cavity occlusion. Main ceramic maps are 2048px, secondary maps 512px. Color is sRGB; data maps are linear. Original baked PNGs and editable source graphs are retained.

artPass.direction: Preserve approved silhouettes, exact hull bounds and propulsion anchors; strengthen formed panel construction, component-specific bevels and canopy seating. Two-layer nozzle cuffs/petals with recessed pressure sleeve, spring keepers and a central emitter carried by three support baffles. Localized straw/blue heat tint, satin service ceramic, saturated painted livery, dielectric canopy, quiet PBR finish and short-range cavity occlusion/roughness. Original authored geometry and procedural textures; no external assets.

finishPass.runtimeTextures: Embedded lossless PNG, Blender glTF channel packing
finishPass.construction: Approved envelope and exhaust anchors retained; formed panel sections, service fasteners, component bevels and recessed intake construction.

reviewEvidence: Ignored .experiments/kestrel-blender; root owns durable formal review record.

finishTarget.role: Selected material/construction target only; not a UV atlas or runtime asset. Silhouette remains the previously approved chassis.
finishTarget.input: Actual Three.js fixed front-three-quarter screenshot of the baseline GLB; saved ship-closeup-v1.png used only for material fidelity.
finishTarget.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create one chosen Kestrel surface-finish target at 2K-class 2048x1280 output. Input 1 is the exact ship/edit target; input 2 is ONLY material-fidelity reference, never shape or lighting. Upgrade this exact ship's surface finish. Preserve silhouette, proportions, canopy, twin engine count, vermilion markings, camera and background. Show formed ceramic panels, graphite structure, machined metal, restrained edge wear, directional fine scratches and dirt in recesses. Preserve clean areas and readable neutral lighting. No new appendages, dramatic relighting, depth-of-field concealment or redesigned ship. Make main panel thickness, bevel highlights, recessed service joints and fasteners believable at this distance; satin ceramic, graphite and titanium must read distinctly. Keep the original 07 marking unchanged. Preserve all geometry outline and studio framing.
